pr.title: Answer the band's questions through discuss, and drop the tracked-file argument
pr.head: 3996ae6e0d16bc6c55372d5d76e4896d777a0911

summary: Projector's band is the strip a Claude Code plugin draws above the prompt. It lists the pull requests the session's loops track and the session's inbox: questions an agent asked you with the ask tool, and notices it posted with tell. Clicking an item opens its drawer, which shows the detail, a question's numbered options, and three actions: discuss, dismiss, and snooze.

Before this change, a question's drawer offered two ways to answer in your own words: a "Type something" field, and discuss. Discuss put the quoted question and a space in the prompt, so anything you typed after it sat on the quote's line and was never recorded as an answer. This change removes the field and makes discuss the way to give a free answer. Discuss now fills the quoted question followed by a blank line; whatever you type under it and send becomes the question's typed answer, through the same sent-prompt reader that options already used.

The change also drops /projector <tracked file>, which let a session list a loop another session runs. To learn that file's kind, the band scanned every process on the machine with ps -A. Now the band lists only the watchers its own session starts, and /projector only shows or hides the band.

The rest are small fixes found while using the band: muted text in the theme's subtle color, the pull request drawer's discuss as a plain Button, the band's clock moving before a hidden band returns, a blank line after GitHub's error, claim renewal that survives a store read past the CLI's timeout, a 30-second window for resolved items, and closing a question's drawer once a sent prompt answers it.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Band: the plugin's strip above the Claude Code prompt.
  • Drawer: the detail an item or pull request row opens under itself.
  • Quote: an item's subject in double quotes, as quoteOf writes it; a sent prompt answers a question by quoting it.
  • Tracked file: the --tracked file a loop's watcher reads, listing the pull requests that loop follows.
  • Claim: a lease on a recorded answer that the band takes while it delivers the answer, and renews while it waits.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:

  • The review of f90f55d suggested that a watcher replace a kindless seen loop an earlier version kept. a2e2d10 does that.
  • One finding is open: the in-progress inbox plan, docs/projects/inbox/readme.md, still describes discuss as "the quoted subject and a space" and a one-minute window. The author agreed and will take the rewrite from #294 by merging main once it lands.

groups.title: Discuss answers a question in your own words
groups.kicker: The free-text field goes, and discuss leaves a blank line to type the answer under
intro: A question is answered by a prompt you send that quotes it: answersIn finds each open question's quote that ends its line and takes the next non-blank line as the answer. If that line matches an option, the option's letter is recorded; otherwise it is recorded as a typed answer under the letter after the last option.

The old discuss left the quote followed by a space, and the reader required the quote to be followed directly by a newline, so an answer typed under a discussed question was dropped. Now discuss fills "quote"\n\n, and the reader also accepts spaces or tabs between the quote and its line's end. Text typed on the quote's own line still answers nothing, so you can still talk a question over without answering it.

With discuss carrying free answers, the drawer's Input field is gone. The drawer stays open while you type, so the options and detail stay in view, and closes once a sent prompt answers its question. Opened again, a resolved question's drawer lists a typed answer after the options, numbered and marked ✓.

checks.text: A discussion typed under the blank line, rather than on the quote's line, is now recorded as the answer. The docs say this, and the test discuss puts the question above a blank line, what you type under it answers, and dismiss resolves it pins it.

files.note: The sent-prompt reader accepts trailing spaces or tabs after a quote, and resolved items stay 30 seconds instead of a minute.

checks.text: The quote can match mid-line, as before; only what follows it is checked. after.replace(/^\s*\n/, '') then skips the blank line discuss leaves.

This docstring and the one on answersIn now match the code: RESOLVED_MS is 30 seconds, and both an option and discuss leave the quote ending its line. Checked by reading both against the functions they describe.

groups.title: The band lists only its own session's loops
groups.kicker: No more hand-named tracked files and no process scan
intro: A loop is one of Projector's background watchers, such as watch-prs.sh for a review loop. The band learns a loop when the session runs its watcher and records the watcher's tracked file and kind in session state.

Before, /projector <tracked file> added a file by hand, with no kind; the band then ran ps -A to find the watcher reading it and borrow its kind. This change deletes that command argument, the runningLoops scan, and expandPath, which parsed the typed path. Session state from an earlier version can still hold a hand-named entry with no kind, so load filters to entries whose kind is known, and remember replaces such an entry when this session starts a watcher on the same file.

files.note: Removes the tracked-file argument and the process scan, and carries the drawer, color, clock, and claim fixes in the next group.

checks.text: remember counts a path as seen only when an entry with a kind tracks it, and swaps a kindless entry for the watcher's. The test leaves out a tracked file an earlier version was given by hand, until the session starts its watcher checks the stored list; it passes at this head.
The toast no longer points at the removed /projector <tracked file>; it says the band leaves that loop out.

closeDrawer runs only for the questions this prompt answered, and only once the prompt has entered. It closes the drawer even when answerFromPrompt later fails to record the answer, which leaves the question open with its drawer closed.

files.note: Deletes expandPath, whose only caller was the removed command argument.
SeenLoop.kind is now required, since every new entry comes from a watcher.

groups.title: Smaller band fixes
groups.kicker: Colors, the pull request drawer, the clock, error spacing, and claim renewal
intro:
• Muted text uses subtle. dimColor draws at full strength in some terminals, so the divider, resolved items and options, the | separators, and the pull request drawer's facts take the theme's subtle color.
  • The pull request drawer's discuss is a plain Button. A Markdown link took no Enter on the main screen; a Button does.
  • Showing the band moves its clock first. show sets the band's now before it shows, so an item whose snooze ended while the band was hidden draws at once instead of after GitHub answers.
  • A blank line follows GitHub's error when items come under it.
  • A store read that times out no longer skips claim renewal. checkInbox catches a failed readStore, so renewClaims still runs and a waiting answer's claim does not lapse.
  • A sent answer closes its question's drawer. The new closeDrawer helper, which snooze also uses, returns the band to its list once the prompt has entered.

checks.text: Ran claude plugin test . at this head: 71 pass, 0 fail. The new tests cover each fix, including a hung inbox list that still renews claims and a snooze that ends while the band is hidden.

groups.title: Documentation
groups.kicker: The plugin guide describes the new discuss and drops the tracked-file argument
intro: docs/plugins.md describes discuss as the way to answer in your own words, says the drawer stays open while you type and closes once you send the answer, drops the field from the drawer example and /projector <tracked file> from the band section, splits the drawer's actions into a list, and corrects the drawer's extra room to two rows, only in a terminal.
